newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese bonds close off highs after rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese bonds close off highs after rate cut.

text.p: Portuguese bonds closed off highs after the Bank of Portugal's modest repo rate cut and dealers said they could correct further in line with Bonos tomorrow.
"Futures and cash bonds slipped at the close and eased off the highs in sympathy with Spain after the timid 15 basis point repo rate cut by the Bank of Portugal," an operator said.

"Considering the present differences between Portuguese and Spanish official rates, the negative yield spreads are wide. This makes the local market weak, especially if Spanish bonds start selling again," another dealer said.
The Bank of Portugal has room to cut the repo rate further to between 6.80 and 7.00 percent by the end of the year, analysts said.

"If optimism over Portugal's chances of qualifying for the European single currency persists, if the escudo continues to rise and if inflation eases in the coming months as expected, the Bank of Portugal will cut its rates again," Isabel Cabral, economist with Lisbon broker Fincor, told Reuters.
